says: In next/, the T1a walk starts a request on a stalled pair in the background and then waits at most 1000 scheduler turns for its start letter to land; the runner hashes every input with crypto.subtle.digest on libuv's thread pool first, so on a busy machine the turns run out, the walk never records the request as current, and L9 or L8 fails when that request later completes.
proof: CI: PR 1224's run 43620712520, job next (5), at f67fc0e7f: `L9: only the current reference completes a request: expected 'BODYKCJMBFYESN "x"/ü-2-2' to be undefined`, seed 119120, path "11". Run 43601969237, job next (4): L8 on path "53". Local trace of path "11" on Node 26.13.0: start k=2 ref -2-2 runs with pair 2 stalled and lands in 2 turns. A probe on the wait counted 1 to 3 turns idle; with shard 5's heaviest files beside it at --maxWorkers=3 and CI=true, one start took 163 turns and another 139, and an async_hooks probe on that one saw 138 Immediate callbacks, one HASHREQUEST and one PROMISE over 21.6 ms: the background was parked on the WebCrypto digest from inputDigest (next/packages/libfabrika/src/runtime/Runner.ts:277). Red on unchanged code: `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--import=<a module that keeps pbkdf2 jobs of about 46 ms running in each test worker>` with `vitest run next/packages/libfabrika/src/node/ProgramMailRuntime.test.ts -t 'T1a [secrets]' --maxWorkers=1` failed `L8: a missing name is a typed refusal` on seed 119120, path "0". Green after the fix with the same load: both T1a laws passed.
cost: Any pull request whose CI shard runs ProgramMailRuntime.test.ts can go red on the fixed seed when the runner is busy, with a failure that names a law and looks like a product bug, and never fails on a laptop.
